item.title: Informe desde Quibdó: De la Espriella anuncia plan de reconstrucción del Chocó
item.description: El presidente de Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella, visitó el departamento del Chocó, la región que fue epicentro de uno de los terremotos más fuertes que ha sacudido a Colombia en su historia. Más de cuatro días después, De la Espriella anunció un plan de reconstrucción basado en un gerente especial que él mismo designará para la región. Por su parte, las autoridades departamentales han hecho un llamado a crear un banco de materiales que se necesitan para la reconstrucción. Desde Quibdó, nos informa nuestro enviado especial, Julián Ramírez. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Europe's mountain summits are warming—vegetation is responding in surprisingly different ways
item.description: Decades of climate change have not left Europe's mountain vegetation unscathed. However, the changes observed do not always match expectations. As a new international study by a research team led by researchers from the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the BOKU University shows, alpine vegetation has shifted significantly towards warmth-associated species. However, the direct link between this so-called thermophilization and local warming is surprisingly weak. The study has recently been published in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bound gravitational waves inspired by photonic systems
item.description: When one mentions "waves," we immediately think of a perturbation that propagates. This applies to waves on the shore, sound waves in the air or electromagnetic waves that we use to transmit information via optical fibers. The same idea of propagating perturbations applies to gravitational waves (GWs), which entered the mainstream media a decade ago after their first direct detection. These are perturbations of the elastic fabric that we are all embedded in, called spacetime. Fuente: Phys.org.
